subject: Post-demo: recommended models, eval assets & rollback / pin options
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Young <sophie.young@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: recommended models, eval assets & rollback / pin options

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so you have everything in one place.

Recap (what we covered)
- Primary goal: replace on-prem heuristic rewrite pipeline with an LLM-assisted extraction + normalization flow for product attributes (title, brand, color).
- Key constraints: low latency at inference (95th < 250ms), deterministic behavior for top-shelf SKUs, and strict PII-inference separation.
- Concern you raised: a version update last month changed tokenization slightly and caused a ~4% drop in exact-match on a critical SKU subset.

Recommended models & quick rationale
- redwood-v2.7-instruct-qa (baseline): best latency/quality trade-off for short product titles.
- redwood-quant-2.7-8bit (cost-optimized): candidate for bulk embedding and background enrichment jobs.
- redwood-specialized-extract-1.3 (structured extractions): highest schema fidelity on our internal evals for attribute extraction.

Assets attached
- eval-benchmarks.csv — slice-level metrics from the demo prompts (precision/recall/emd per SKU bucket).
- prompt-sets_v1.zip — canonical prompts + negative cases and guardrail patterns.
- mutual-action-plan-ATLAS.docx — proposed timeline and responsibilities.

Quality & regression guardrails (explicit suggestions)
1) Version pinning: we recommend pinning the production route to redwood-v2.7-instruct-qa@2026-01-12 for the first 2 weeks after rollout; that variant is included in the eval csv.
2) Canary + shadow: enable a 5% canary against the new variant with shadow logging for a head-to-head diff.
3) Regressions: if the canary shows >2% drop on any critical slice we auto-rollback the canary variant (we can define slices together).
4) Emergency rollback SLA: our Dedicated customers can get a 30-minute rollback window; for Hosted we can commit to a 2-hour rollback plan for production routes with an agreed MRP.

Ask / next steps
- Sophie: please confirm the primary SKU slice we should track (I noted: electronics > top-shelf, color-sensitive SKUs).
- Procurement: looped if you want a draft SOW for the Dedicated pilot; otherwise we’ll proceed on the standard trial path.
- I’ll schedule a short 30-min follow-up next week to lock the pin/rollout plan and share a one-click eval run you can execute against a holdout set.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
attachments: eval-benchmarks.csv (CSV, 1.2MB); prompt-sets_v1.zip (ZIP, 240KB); mutual-action-plan-ATLAS.docx (DOCX, 120KB)
From: Sophie Young <sophie.young@atlasretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended models, eval assets & rollback / pin options

Mina —

Appreciate the clear recap and the assets. Reviewing the CSV now — quick clarifying notes:
- The SKU slice I care most about is "Electronics > Headphones" (ASIN-like pattern). That is where the last rollout caused the downstream mismatch.
- We do need deterministic outputs for the product title field; small tokenization shifts broke several downstream joins.

Questions:
1) Can you confirm the pin ID you mentioned (redwood-v2.7-instruct-qa@2026-01-12) is still available and if there is a cost difference to pin vs running the latest hosted?
2) If we request the Dedicated pilot + rollback SLA, what is the typical lead time to provision the reserved capacity?

Procurement — if you want a draft SOW to review, I can schedule a time next week to go over numbers.

– Sophie
Director, Product Data Platform | Atlas Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 20:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended models, eval assets & rollback / pin options

Looping you both — internal ops plan to propose to Atlas:

1) Pin confirmation and cost note
- We can reserve redwood-v2.7-instruct-qa@2026-01-12 for Atlas. Pin pricing: +8% unit cost on hosted per-token vs non-pinned latest (covers storage and version escrow).

2) Dedicated pilot provisioning
- Typical lead time: 7–10 business days for initial capacity (can be expedited to 72 hours with an on-call infra approval and initial commit).
- SLA add-on for automated rollback and 30-min intervention is available as an enterprise add-on.

3) Technical approach for regression detection
- Karthik: propose we share an eval harness (one-click) that runs the prompt set against both the pinned variant and candidate variant and emits slice diffs and HTML visual report. We already have the visualization in the eval app.
- For the canary: run 5% traffic through candidate variant for 48 hours and compare per-slice EM/precision. If we see >2% EM drop on "Headphones" slice, auto-fallback.

4) Ask to Mina
- Please attach the minimal holdout (10–50 examples) for the headphone slice so Karthik can baseline the harness.

I’ll prepare a short pricing note for procurement and a provisioning checklist.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Young <sophie.young@atlasretail.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended models, eval assets & rollback / pin options

Sophie / team —

Thanks for the quick response. A couple concrete items from the platform/SE side:

- I created a shareable eval run in the Redwood Eval app with the prompt set you sent and the pinned variant redwood-v2.7-instruct-qa@2026-01-12. Link: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/atlas-2026 (shared in metadata). The run compares pinned vs candidate (latest) and includes per-slice diffs and example-level traces.

- Attachments: I added a short sample holdout of 30 headphone SKUs into the Drive folder; please confirm I can run it (drive link in related_links). If you want, we can red-team a few adversarial titles.

- Rollback mechanics (how it works)
  1) Pin route to the specified variant. If the canary crosses the threshold, we trigger an automated route swap to the pinned variant; this is near-instant for Hosted and sub-5 minutes for Dedicated with warm instances.
  2) For full traffic rollback we preserve request logs and allow a forensic diff; if forensic analysis requires model-level changes we can stage a frozen variant and run A/B.

- Next step proposal
  * Today / Tomorrow: Sophie — confirm the headphone holdout (I ran a dry-run on our side and the diff is visible in the eval app).
  * Early next week: schedule 30-min call to finalize pin + provisioning timeline and share procurement pricing.

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful. I’ll also export a short HTML diff report and upload to the Drive folder.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
